purpose: Engineering de-risk of B-CAP on real producer code (Colab T4, code-with-citation permission): prove the capacity observation extension trains and reaches the policy. NOT a scientific result.
executed_by: Codex GPU-track lead on a disposable Colab VM, terminated after the run; producer data never moved; producer source neither archived nor modified locally; repository and external clones unchanged.

treatments: 17-D control: randomized RSU capacity hidden from the actor
19-D B-CAP: explicit normalized capacity plus selected-RSU headroom in the observation
design.scale: 4,992 steps / 312 MAPPO updates per treatment; one seed; two episodes per capacity level in diagnostics
design.environment: producer synthetic training environment (not Manchester traces; its completion/latency numbers are not comparable to trace-evaluation numbers)

measured.control_17d_fixed_capacity_diagnostic: exactly invariant across all four capacity levels
measured.bcap_19d_fixed_capacity_diagnostic: local/V2I decisions change with capacity — the new observations reach the policy
measured.bcap_19d_short_run_performance: no improvement at this scale: ~98.86% completion / 37.5 ms latency vs 99.24% / 33.44 ms control

interpretation_limits: Engineering smoke only: one seed, minutes-scale training, synthetic environment — not a scientific null, not dissertation evidence, no admission performed.

The 17-D invariance under randomized-but-hidden capacity independently reproduces the observability-gap mechanism in a from-scratch policy: blindness follows from the observation design, not from one checkpoint.

The 19-D behavioural response proves plumbing, not benefit; the real B-CAP experiment requires its own predeclaration, full-scale training, checkpoint homecoming through the pinned-actor review, and instrument evaluation.
